nodes.summary: Let $a$, $m$, $b$, $d$ be natural numbers, and let $p$ and $q$ be lists of comparators on wires indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, where every comparator of $p$ joins two wires in $[a, m)$ and every comparator of $q$ joins two wires in $[m, b)$. If $p$ and $q$ both have depth at most $d$, then the concatenation of $p$ followed by $q$ also has depth at most $d$: the two lists run in parallel.
nodes.title: Parallel composition of comparator lists on adjacent blocks

nodes.summary: If a list $p$ of comparators on wires indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ has depth at most $d$ and a list $q$ of comparators has depth at most $e$, then the concatenation of $p$ followed by $q$ has depth at most $d + e$.
nodes.title: Depth of sequential composition of comparator lists

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, Batcher's bitonic sorting network on $2^k$ wires has depth at most $d$ for some natural number $d$ with $2d \le k(k+1)$; that is, its depth is at most $k(k+1)/2$.
nodes.title: Batcher's bitonic sorting network has depth at most $k(k+1)/2$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a list of comparators on wires indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. Let $S$ assign to each wire a finite set of natural numbers and let $\ell$ assign to each wire a natural number, such that $|S(x)| \le 2^{\ell(x)}$ for every wire $x$. For each wire $x$, let $L(x)$ be the level of $x$ after $p$ starting from the levels $\ell$. Then for every wire $x$, the influence set of $x$ after $p$ starting from $S$ has at most…
nodes.title: Influence sets grow at most exponentially with the level

nodes.summary: A comparator network on $n$ wires has depth at most $d$ when its list of comparators, read as pairs of wire numbers in $\mathbb{N}$, has depth at most $d$: starting with every wire at level $0$ and scheduling each comparator one level after the later of its two wires, every wire ends at level at most $d$.
nodes.title: Depth bound for a comparator network

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $b$, the bitonic merger on the block of $2^k$ wires $b, b + 1, \dots, b + 2^k - 1$ has depth at most $k$.
nodes.title: The bitonic merger has depth at most $k$

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $b$, the comparator list of Batcher's bitonic sorter on the block of $2^k$ wires $b, b + 1, \dots, b + 2^k - 1$ has depth at most $d$ for some natural number $d$ with $2d \le k(k+1)$; that is, its depth is at most $k(k+1)/2$.
nodes.title: Depth of the bitonic sorter's comparator list

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $b$, the half-cleaner on the block of $2m$ wires $b, \dots, b + 2m - 1$ has depth at most $1$: its comparators join pairwise disjoint pairs of wires.
nodes.title: The half-cleaner has depth at most $1$

nodes.summary: A list of comparators on wires indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ has depth at most $d$ when, starting with every wire at level $0$ and scheduling each comparator one level after the later of its two wires, every wire ends at level at most $d$.
nodes.title: Depth bound for a comparator list

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p$ be a list of comparators, each joining two wires in $[0, n)$, and let $f$ assign a Boolean value to each wire in $\mathbb{N}$. If $f(y)$ is false for some $y < n$, then after running $p$ on $f$ some wire $y < n$ carries the value false.
nodes.title: Comparators inside $(0, n)$ keep a false value inside $(0, n)$

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a list of natural numbers of length $N$ and let $ps$ be a list of comparators all of whose wires lie in $[0, N)$. Extend $t$ to all wires by setting $t_y = 0$ for $y \ge N$. Then for every wire $x$, the entry at position $x$ of the tabulated levels of $ps$ starting from the table $t$ (read as $0$ when $x \ge N$) equals the level of wire $x$ after $ps$, starting from the initial levels $y \mapsto t_y$.
nodes.title: Tabulated levels agree with levels

nodes.summary: Given a list $ps$ of comparators on wires indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ and an assignment $S$ of a finite set of natural numbers to each wire, the influence sets after $ps$ are computed by processing the comparators in order: a comparator $(i, j)$ replaces the current sets of both wires $i$ and $j$ by their union, and leaves the sets of all other wires unchanged. Starting from $S(x) = \{x\}$, the set of a wire tracks the…
nodes.title: Influence sets of wires

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $d$, if Batcher's bitonic sorting network on $2^k$ wires has depth at most $d$, then $k \le d$.
nodes.title: Batcher's bitonic sorter on $2^k$ wires has depth at least $k$

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $d$, if the comparator list of Batcher's bitonic sorter on the wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$ has depth at most $d$, then $k \le d$.
nodes.title: The bitonic sorting comparator list on $2^k$ wires has depth at least $k$

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a comparator network on $n$ wires and $d$ a natural number. If $C$ sorts every Boolean input (its output is monotone in the wire order for every input in $\{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^n$, with $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$) and $C$ has depth at most $d$, then $n \le 2^d$.
nodes.title: Every sorting network on $n$ wires has depth at least $\log_2 n$

nodes.summary: Let $ps$ be a list of comparators on wires indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, all of whose wires lie in $[0, n)$, and let $d$ be a natural number. Suppose that for every Boolean input $v$ on the wires $0, \dots, n - 1$, extended by $\mathrm{false}$ to the wires $\ge n$, the output $w$ of $ps$ satisfies $w_i \le w_j$ whenever $i \le j < n$ (with $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$). If $ps$ has depth at most $d$, then $n \le 2^d$.
nodes.title: Sorting comparator lists on $n$ wires have depth at least $\log_2 n$

nodes.summary: Let $ps$ be a list of comparators all of whose wires lie in $[a, b)$, and let $\ell, \ell' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be initial levels that agree on every wire in $[a, b)$. Then for every wire $x$ in $[a, b)$, the level of $x$ after $ps$ starting from $\ell$ equals the level of $x$ after $ps$ starting from $\ell'$.
nodes.title: Levels inside a block depend only on initial levels inside it

nodes.summary: Let $ps$ be a list of comparators all of whose wires lie in $[a, b)$. Then for all initial levels $\ell : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every wire $x$ with $x < a$ or $b \le x$, the level of $x$ after $ps$ starting from $\ell$ is $\ell(x)$.
nodes.title: Comparators inside a block leave levels outside it unchanged

nodes.summary: For every list $ps$ of comparators and all initial levels $\ell : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the levels after the list obtained from $ps$ by replacing each comparator $(i, j)$ with $(j, i)$, starting from $\ell$, equal the levels after $ps$ starting from $\ell$.
nodes.title: Swapping the wires of every comparator does not change levels

nodes.summary: Given a list $ps$ of comparators and a table $t$ of natural numbers $t_0, \dots, t_{N-1}$, the tabulated levels are computed by processing the comparators in order: a comparator $(i, j)$ sets both entries $t_i$ and $t_j$ to $\max(t_i, t_j) + 1$, where an entry outside the table reads as $0$ and a write outside the table is ignored.
nodes.title: Tabulated levels

nodes.summary: Given a list of comparators on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires, each a pair $(i, j)$ of wires, and a starting level $\ell(x)$ for every wire $x$, process the comparators in order, keeping a current level for each wire, initially $\ell$: a comparator $(i, j)$ whose wires currently have levels $a$ and $b$ sets the current levels of both wires $i$ and $j$ to $\max(a, b) + 1$ and leaves every other level unchanged. The…
nodes.title: Comparator levels under earliest scheduling

nodes.summary: Let $f_0, g_0 : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be two inputs with values in a linear order $\alpha$, let $S$ assign to each wire $x$ a finite set $S(x)$ of input positions, and let $F, G : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be wire values such that for every wire $x$, if $f_0$ and $g_0$ agree on $S(x)$, then $F(x) = G(x)$. Then for every list of comparators and every wire $x$, if $f_0$ and $g_0$ agree on the influence set of $x$…
nodes.title: Outputs depend only on the influence set

nodes.summary: The comparators of a network on $n$ wires, in order, with each comparator $(i, j)$ written as the pair of natural numbers $(i, j)$, forgetting that $i, j < n$.
nodes.title: Comparator list of a network
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
